tools.name: inspect_site_tracking
tools.description: Performs a bounded, non-persisting GET of an authorized public domain's homepage and reports tracker markup, consent setup signals, and runtime-verification gaps. It does not run JavaScript, submit forms, create a RegSentry record, or make a legal determination.

tools.name: interpret_consent_evidence
tools.description: Deterministically grades a redacted set of tracker-request observations by consent phase. It computes from the supplied data only, stores nothing, and returns a technical—not legal—interpretation.

tools.name: get_remediation_playbook
tools.description: Returns deterministic, tracker-specific consent-gating guidance from RegSentry's maintained playbooks. It does not change a website, contact a vendor, or verify that a fix was implemented.

tools.name: inspect_runtime_consent
tools.description: Visits an authorized public homepage in three isolated browser sessions and records known tracker request attempts before consent and after exact reject-all or accept-all buttons. Uses temporary browser sessions, blocks non-GET requests, supplies no user credentials, and reports missing controls and

tools.name: compare_consent_observations
tools.description: Compares two supplied RegSentry runtime snapshots of the same domain, phase by phase. Marks missing controls and incomplete observations unresolved. Reports newly observed or no-longer-observed tracker attempts without claiming causation, compliance or a verified fix. Stores nothing and makes no net

tools.name: export_consent_report
tools.description: Formats a supplied RegSentry runtime snapshot as a private plain-text report with its date, method, phase results and limitations. Returns file content without publishing, sharing, or storing it. Does not turn supplied evidence into a compliance certificate or legal opinion.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "inspect_runtime_consent" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
